name: golden-journey-v1-context-drop
description: RED baseline for A12 (prior-turn context continuity). SYNTHETIC (hand-authored) transcript of the lived continuity defect: the draft and analysis establish the option labels and the leader, then the follow-up turn ('how does the runner-up compare?') answers as if the conversation never happened. It denies having the earlier results and names no option established in prior turns. A12 must FAIL on step 4_follow_up and the replay must exit 1. Before A12 existed, this fixture exited 0 (its only fail was advisory A5) - proof that A1-A11 alone could not catch a dropped conversation. Pre/post replay transcripts are archived durably in Docs/golden-journey/a12-continuity-invariant-evidence.md.
brief: We are a 15-person engineering team weighing three options for scaling delivery over the next six months: hire two senior engineers locally, engage an offshore partner, or introduce tiered pricing to hire more gradually. Decision matters for Q3 roadmap commitments.

expected_milestones.expect: A12 fails: the answer denies prior context and references no option or factor established in earlier turns

transcript.note: Synthetic continuity-drop capture. Steps 1-3 are healthy; step 4 drops the conversation.

body.assistant_text: Your decision model is ready, with three options and a few cost and delivery factors. You can run the analysis whenever you're ready, or refine the options first.
Analysis complete. Hire two senior engineers currently leads with about 62% probability against the goal, ahead of Engage an offshore partner.
Hire two senior engineers leads at roughly 62% because it improves delivery speed most directly while keeping Budget within range.

I don't have the earlier results in this conversation, so I can't tell you which option was the runner-up or how it compares. In general, comparing two approaches means weighing their trade-offs against what you are trying to achieve. If you share the details again, I can take a look.
